messages:
incident-bot: Pager: latency_alert service=redwood-inference-api region=eu-west2 metric=p99_latency value=780ms threshold=500ms — paging oncall
oncall-sre: acked, I'm on it. grabbing dashboards now. @maria can you check interzone metrics? :eyes:
maria: looking — p95 up to ~220ms, p99 spike to 700-900ms across streaming endpoints. tail looks like streaming stalls + TLS handshake retries. seeing a spike starting 3698765300.
jun: saw increased connection resets to NAT gateway in eu-west2-a -> eu-west2-b paths. Packet loss counters tick up around same time.
net-eng: adding context: we've been rolling a fw rule change in eu-west2 this morning but it finished before the spike. I'll check route table churn.
oncall-sre: can we reproduce with internal loadgen? if it's cross-AZ only maybe routing/NAT.
infra-ops: running `tcpdump` on a couple streaming-front instances now, attaching quick sample. will paste relevant lines if we see TLS retransmit loops.
maria: logs show many clients hitting 502/504-ish stream disconnects then immediate reconnects. prefix cache hits drop ~20% during spike.
jun: NAT ephemeral port exhaustion pattern looks plausible — lots of short-lived client connections from upstream -> NAT running out, causing SYN retries, TLS handshake retries.
net-eng: confirming high conntrack counts on vGW nodes. `conntrack -S` shows syn_sent retran > normal. Also DNS queries show retries — maybe HOL on DNS from retransmits.
oncall-sre: severity? impacting streaming tail latency and some customers seeing stalls. Escalate to SEs for customer notice? @tess please draft a short notice if we keep mitigation.
tess: will draft. summarize impact and ETA in 10.
infra-ops: quick mitigation attempt: enabling additional NAT capacity pool and bumping ephemeral port range on affected NAT instances. applying now.
net-eng: also temporarily pinned routing to prefer eu-west2-b via alternate transit (reroute) to avoid noisy path — applying BGP local-pref tweak.
oncall-sre: nice. list commands you ran?
infra-ops: ran:
```
# increase ephemeral ports on nat instance
sysctl -w net.ipv4.ip_local_port_range="1024 65000"
# increase conntrack table size
sysctl -w net.netfilter.ip_conntrack_max=262144
# spin up warm spare NAT node
terraform apply -var region=eu-west2 -target=module.nat_pool[eu-west2].aws_instance.warm_spare
```
jun: after bump, conntrack free went up and SYN retransmits dropped ~80% within 30s. p99 started sliding down.
maria: prefix cache hit rate recovering slowly. streaming sessions that didn't time out resumed. customer-side retries still in flight for a few minutes.
net-eng: routed path switch confirmed. BGP local-pref rollback planned after stabilization. watching for packet loss on original path.
oncall-sre: monitoring: p95 ~180ms, p99 ~320ms and falling. still above normal but trending.
tess: draft posted to customers: "We're investigating elevated streaming latency in eu-west2 caused by cross-AZ network path and NAT capacity pressure. Mitigation in progress; services are recovering. We'll update in 15 minutes." want any edits?
maria: add note that no data loss observed, just transient stalls and reconnects.
tess: updated.
incident-bot: Incident created: INC-2026-369876 — impact: partial streaming stalls in eu-west2, scope: subset of customers behind NAT gateway pools.
oncall-sre: next actions: continue watch for 30m, collect histograms for TLS handshake times, surface any failing customers to SE.
infra-ops: collecting `ss -ntap` / `conntrack -L` dumps and saving to s3: s3://redwood-ops/incidents/3698765432/
jun: also check DNS cache server load — noticed increased response latency from our internal resolvers during the spike. might be cascading due to retries.
net-eng: investigating if FW rollout earlier left asymmetric path causing bufferbloat. capturing pcap at edge to correlate.
maria: alert rule suggestion: add ephemeral-port-utilization metric and alert at 80% to avoid this class of issue.
oncall-sre: agree, ticket that to postmortem.
tess: customers notified. any need for immediate rollback of recent fw change? net-eng: fw change not correlated by timeline, but we'll keep it as rollback candidate.
jun: marking this paging as handoff to oncall-sre for next shift — add to oncall notes: cause=nat-ephemeral-pressure + interzone packetloss; mitigation=increase-ephemeral-range + scale-nat + route-reroute; followups=postmortem+alerting+capacity-testing.
oncall-sre: acknowledged handoff. will add to incident timeline and include metric graphs.
incident-bot: Reminder: please run postmortem template after incident closed: /playbooks/postmortem-template.md :memo:
maria: one last note — streaming tail stalls disproportionately affected sessions with short-lived connections (websocket-ish patterns). consider sticky connections or connection pooling as longer-term mitigation.
oncall-sre: good. thanks all for quick move. keep watch for 15m then we can close if stable. :thumbsup:
